specification.objective: Make the PostgreSQL parallel-checkin test deterministic by freezing the service clock after the fixture seeds its punches, without changing runtime behavior.

requirements.statement: After the PostgreSQL fixture seeds the database, freeze app.services.time_clock.utcnow to one second after emp-04's latest seeded punch before launching concurrent check-ins.
The concurrency test continues proving exactly one of two parallel check-ins succeeds and exactly one new check-in is persisted.
Only the PostgreSQL test harness changes; application code, migrations, schemas, and production behavior remain untouched.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The test derives a fixed UTC timestamp from the seeded latest emp-04 punch and monkeypatches app.services.time_clock.utcnow before starting worker threads.
With the isolated READ COMMITTED PostgreSQL database configured, test_postgres_parallel_checkins_are_serialized passes and observes results ['conflict', 'ok'] plus exactly one additional check-in.
No production file changes; all other time-clock integrity tests pass on both the committed baseline and the corrected test tree.

invariants.statement: The fixed test timestamp is strictly later than the latest seeded punch and identical for both concurrent workers.
The test never relies on wall-clock time being later than sample data generated for the current day.

forbidden_states.statement: The test reaches the concurrency assertion with both operations rejected because the wall clock precedes the seeded latest punch.
Production code or data-seeding behavior changes to accommodate the test.

inputs.statement: The isolated PostgreSQL fixture seeds emp-04 punches before yielding its session factory; the parallel test submits two new check-ins after fixture setup.

outputs.statement: A deterministic PostgreSQL check-in concurrency test that tests row-lock serialization rather than host wall-clock ordering.

failure_semantics.statement: The affected PostgreSQL test must return one ok and one conflict and persist exactly one additional check-in; setup, missing-URL, or isolation-guard failures are not passes.
